analysis:
Reviewed the base text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md (lines 386-1236) against the patch excerpt. The PR is documentation-only. It adds (a) a statement at head ~1210 that, after the drain, shutdown waits up to 15 s for each model's unload and leaves a model whose native retirement never completes to process exit (`ProviderLoop.unloadAllModelsForShutdown`), and (b) status documentation for a restart-needed notice when saved `enabled_models` differs from the applied filter (`enabled_models_at_start`, `enabled_models_at_last_switch`), plus a retry-on-memory-pressure line that is cut off in the excerpt. No code, controls, endpoints or trust boundaries change here.

Security relevance: the bounded unload relates to T-028 (residual GPU/KV data) and T-029/T-010 (availability). The doc says a stuck model is left to process exit, so plaintext KV/GPU memory persists until the process ends. That is consistent with the existing OS-level residual-memory posture. The doc does not claim a wipe, so it is not an overclaim. Whether the 15 s bound is actually implemented in `ProviderLoop.unloadAllModelsForShutdown` is not visible and should be checked in any source-bearing batch.

The status doc change is informational and exposes only model-selection config diffs to the local operator. It does not touch token, issuer, App Attest or cache-storage handling. The unchanged logout (T-053, A-008), sandbox installer (TB-013/T-061) and addon hold (TB-012) text in the base appears unmodified; the changed ranges are 1287-1291 base and 1210-1212/1290-1305 head. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the remainder of the status bullet rewrite was not seen. The rest of the head hunk (up to 1305) should be checked for any security-relevant claim. No findings.
